analysis: The PR changes only scripts/test-docs-impact-check.py. It removes the "retained console" case from the cases dict (base line 43) and removes test_retained_console_telemetry_keeps_both_documentation_obligations (base lines 88-94). This matches a removal of the "retained console" rule from scripts/docs-impact-rules.json, which is not in the supplied batch. The change is test-only CI tooling. It has no runtime provider, coordinator, crypto, attestation, cache or key-handling effect, so it does not touch the TB-002, TB-003, TB-007 or TB-011 boundaries or T-041's cache controls. The surviving tests still assert that every rule in the rules file has a case (line 46 head), that the cache storage rules require their docs (lines 59-64), that the CLI fails closed without docs (lines 93-106), and that the maintainer override still works. The rule set and test set stay consistent only if the rules file was changed to match. Console-ui telemetry changes would no longer be forced to update console documentation, which is a documentation-process concern rather than a security control. I could not verify the rules file or the docs-impact workflow here, so that is the remaining integration question. I found no security regression.
